$comment: The trust root for offline verification. A verifier trusts THIS file from a clean checkout, never the RELEASE-PUBLIC-KEY.pem bundled inside a package — anyone who can alter a manifest can alter a key sitting next to it. The bundled copy only has to match an entry here.
$keysComment: Empty on purpose. No release signing key has been generated, and inventing a placeholder would make every verification appear to have a trust root when it has none. Until a key is added, dsd:export refuses to sign and dsd:release:verify reports key_id_unknown — both of which are correct.

rotation.policy: One active signing key at a time. Generate the replacement, add it here as active, re-sign nothing — existing packages stay valid under the key that signed them — then mark the previous key revoked once no in-support release depends on it.
rotation.privateKeyLocation: release secret store; never in this repository, never in a package, never in an environment variable that is logged
rotation.generation: openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out dsd-release-<id>.key && openssl pkey -in dsd-release-<id>.key -pubout

revocation.policy: Set status to revoked and record revokedReason. Revocation is deliberately retroactive: every package signed by a revoked key fails verification, because the reason a key is revoked is usually that somebody else may have been able to use it.
onCompromise: Revoke here first, so verification starts failing before anything else is done.
Generate a replacement key and add it as active.
Re-export and re-sign every in-support release from its recorded SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH; a deterministic export reproduces identical bytes, so only the signature changes.
Publish the revocation with the reason. A silent revocation looks like a build error to whoever is verifying.
